# Vanishing reflected-section shifts do not control the normalized overlap

This is an exact obstruction to deriving the residual budget from local
criticality, actual reflected sections, or chord-ratio bounds alone.
The middle fiber is heavy. Global criticality under arbitrary changes
of continuous direction is NOT asserted. In contrast, all three caps
are strict local minima under every ambient normal variation, have
exactly the same mixed mass, and are global minima over every integer
tilt with their respective continuous normal fixed. These distinctions
are part of the result.

The construction is a rational one-parameter family for rational
0<epsilon<=1/100. It gives actual convex fibers A,K,B at -1,0,1,
with (A+B)/2 contained in K, such that the three middle traces form
a positive circuit, all B captures are zero, all A captures are proper,
and the following hold simultaneously:

* Every reflected A section fits in the corresponding actual facet
  of the SAME B with a shift of magnitude at most 8 epsilon.
* The middle chord centroid offsets are at most epsilon^2; their
  lengths remain fixed. Thus their source-centering ratios tend to zero.
* The total missed-A mass divided by |A| is greater than 5/4, uniformly
  separated from 5/4 even as both kinds of shift tend to zero.

Consequently no normalized-overlap continuity estimate based solely on
these shifts can supply the required 5|A|/4 budget. A quantitative use
of the no-heavy or global-depth hypotheses remains necessary.

## 1. Endpoint triangles and their exact sections

Set D=53/5, epsilon in (0,1/100], and

    A=conv{(-10,-10), (3/5+epsilon,3/5-epsilon),
                         (3/5-epsilon,3/5+epsilon)},
    B=T={x<=1, y<=1, x+y>=-1}.

The three caps will be

    H_1={x>=z}, H_2={y>=z}, H_3={-x-y>=z}.          (1)

Their continuous normals (1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1) sum to zero and span
the plane. The B captures are its three supporting edges, hence have
zero area. A has positive area

    a=|A|=2D epsilon,

and each A cut in (1) is proper. The x=-1 A-section is the interval
whose y endpoints are

    l=-1-18 epsilon/(D+epsilon),
    u=-1+18 epsilon/(D-epsilon).

By symmetry the y=-1 section has the same coordinate data. Put

    s=u-l=36D epsilon/(D^2-epsilon^2),
    a_0=(l+u)/2=-1+18 epsilon^2/(D^2-epsilon^2),
    b_0=1-2s,
    delta=a_0+b_0=a_0+1-2s.                         (2)

Here s is the Euclidean length of either axis section. Direct estimates
using D=10.6 and epsilon<=0.01 give

    3 epsilon < s < 4 epsilon,
    0<a_0+1<epsilon^2/5,
    -8 epsilon < delta < 0.                         (3)

On the B edge x=1 select the density 1/2 on the interval

    1-3s <= y <= 1-s

and zero elsewhere. It lies strictly inside the edge -2<=y<=1. Its
mass is s and its centroid has y coordinate b_0. Make the symmetric
choice on y=1. This uses actual subsets of two edges of one triangle;
they are not independent formal facets.

The reflected and shifted A interval is

    -[l,u]+delta=[b_0-s/2,b_0+s/2].                 (4)

It is strictly inside the corresponding B edge, since it is centered
at 1-2s with half-length s/2. Thus delta is the actual reflected-section
translation. Its magnitude tends to zero linearly in epsilon.

On x+y=1, the A section has centroid (1/2,1/2), length
(105 epsilon/53)*sqrt(2), and reflects into the B edge x+y=-1,
whose centroid is (-1/2,-1/2) and length 3sqrt(2). The constant
density 35 epsilon/53 on that B edge has exactly the A-section mass
and opposite centroid. Its reflected-section translation is zero.

## 2. A middle polygon with the required actual chord moments

Fix R=32 and r=16. Define

    c=-s*delta/R, p=r+c, m=-r+c,

and let K_0 be the hexagon, in counterclockwise order,

    (p,0), (0,p), (-r,r), (m,0), (0,m), (r,-r).

From (3),

    0<c<epsilon^2,
    |K_0|=3r^2+c^2>768.                             (5)

The x=0 and y=0 chords have length R and respective centroids (0,c)
and (c,0). The x+y=0 chord has endpoints (-r,r),(r,-r) and centroid
zero. The axis chord moment identity is exactly

    s*a_0+R*c+s*b_0=0,                              (6)

which follows from the definition of c. Thus the actual shift
-(R/s)c is delta, not a freely assigned displacement.

The hexagon contains the diamond |x|+|y|<=r-c: its four vertices lie
on the four actual axis chords. Every vertex midpoint of A and B lies
in [-6,2]^2, hence in |x|+|y|<=12. Since r-c>15, all nine such
midpoints lie inside K_0. Convexity proves

    (A+B)/2 subset K_0.                             (7)

The middle axis chord centering fraction is c/R<epsilon^2/32 and the
third centering fraction is zero. These are much smaller than the
universal planar bound (2-sqrt(3))/2. In particular the ratio of the
shorter to longer source-to-endpoint distances tends to one and exceeds
1/sqrt(3).

## 3. Equalize the three cap masses without changing any cut section

Let alpha_i=|A intersect H_i|, interpreting H_i on base -1. Their
exact values are

    alpha_1=alpha_2=a*(1-81/(D^2-epsilon^2)),
    alpha_3=a*(105/106)^2.

The middle K_0 cap areas are

    q_1=q_2=|K_0|/2+r*c,
    q_3=|K_0|/2-2r*c.

These formulas follow directly by triangulating the captured polygons
with their axis or diagonal chord as one side. Put

    e=alpha_3-alpha_1-3r*c,
    h=e/p.

One has 0<e<22 epsilon. Indeed
81/(D^2-epsilon^2)>0.72 and 1-(105/106)^2<0.02, so
alpha_3-alpha_1>0.70a>14 epsilon, while 3r*c<48epsilon^2.
The upper bound e<a<22epsilon is immediate. Hence h<2epsilon.

Replace the edge from (p,0) to (0,p) by the two segments through

    (p/2+h,p/2+h),

and call the resulting seven-vertex polygon K. The added triangle has
area p*h=e, lies strictly in x>0,y>0,x+y>0, and changes none of the
three source chords. The polygon remains strictly convex. Explicitly,
its seven consecutive oriented turn determinants are

    2h(c+r),
    [(c+r)^2+2h(c-r)]/2,
    c^2+r^2,
    (r-c)^2,
    (r-c)^2,
    c^2+r^2,
    [(c+r)^2+2h(c-r)]/2.

All are positive: c>0, h>0, c<1/10000, h<1/50, and r=16.
Therefore K contains K_0, retains (7), and still has all the stated
chord lengths and centroids.

The bulge adds e to the first two middle cap areas and zero to the
third. All three mixed cap masses are consequently the same number

    Q=q_1+e+alpha_1=q_2+e+alpha_2=q_3+alpha_3.       (8)

The body C=conv({-1}xA union {0}xK union {1}xB) is a full-dimensional
compact convex body in R^3. Its only integer fibers are exactly A,K,B:
the endpoint fibers are immediate, and (7) ensures that the middle
fiber gains nothing outside K from convex combinations of endpoints.

## 4. Strict local minimizing caps under all ambient normal variations

At each cap, the first-order proper-section moment is canceled by the
chosen density on the actual B supporting edge. For the first cap,
the A section has centroid (-1,a_0), the middle chord has centroid
(0,c), and the selected B density has centroid (1,b_0) and mass s.
Equation (6) cancels the continuous moments; the integer moments
cancel because -s+s=0. The second cap is identical by symmetry.
For the third cap, the two endpoint section centroids are opposite,
the middle chord centroid is zero, and the selected B density has
exactly the opposite-endpoint section mass. Its integer moments also
cancel.

The supporting-facet derivative formula therefore writes the derivative
in any normal-perturbation direction, up to the fixed positive factor
1/||u_i||, as

    integral_(F_i) ([ell(w)]_+-theta_i(w)*ell(w)) dH_1(w),       (9)

where ell is the perturbation's affine margin restricted to that edge
in the ambient cap plane. The density theta_i lies strictly between
zero and one on a nondegenerate interval: it is 1/2 on the selected
interval for the first two caps and a constant in (0,1) on the third.
The integrand is nonnegative everywhere and strictly positive wherever
ell is nonzero on that interval. A nonzero affine function cannot
vanish on an interval. Thus (9) is strictly positive for every genuine
change of the projective cap normal. The only zero directions merely
rescale the same cap normal: each lifted B edge spans its two-dimensional
ambient cap plane as vectors from the source.

This proves strict local minimality, not just formal stationarity.
For completeness the first-order expansion is uniform on compact sets
of perturbation directions here. In a fixed neighborhood there are
only finitely many polygon edges; away from their vertices swept strip
areas have the stated linear terms and uniformly quadratic errors.
Within O(t) of a vertex, the moved area is O(t^2), uniformly for unit
normal perturbations. The proper cuts may pass through K vertices,
but the same O(t^2) vertex estimate applies. Compactness of the unit
circle of projective directions makes the strictly positive expression
(9) have a positive minimum. The uniform expansion then makes every
sufficiently small nonzero normal change increase the cap mass.

## 5. Global minimality over all integer tilts at each fixed normal

Keep one of the continuous normals u_i in (1) fixed and replace its
integer coefficient -1 by beta. The endpoint cap thresholds are beta
in A and -beta in B, while the middle cap is unchanged. At beta=-1
the B cap has zero area.

For beta<=-1, the captured A area can only increase and B remains
empty, so the endpoint sum cannot decrease. For -1<=beta<=2 write
t=beta+1 in [0,3]. The exact B captured area is

    3t-t^2/2 >= (3/2)t.                            (10)

All three normalized normals have the same B projection law, as is
also verified by direct triangular sections. The maximum A projection
density for a triangle is twice its area divided by its projection
range: this follows by writing its two affine section-length pieces.
For u_1,u_2 this is at most 4epsilon, and for u_3 at most 2epsilon.
Thus the A area lost after increasing its threshold by t is at most
4epsilon*t. Since 4epsilon<3/2, (10) exceeds that possible loss for
every t>0. Finally beta>=2 captures all of B, whose area 9/2 exceeds
the entire A area a<=53/250. The endpoint sum is therefore globally
minimized at beta=-1. This accounts for every finite integer tilt,
including all supporting and saturated statuses.

## 6. The residual budget nevertheless fails uniformly

The first two missed-A area fractions are

    rho_1=rho_2=81/(D^2-epsilon^2),

and the third is rho_3=1-(105/106)^2. Hence

    kappa=sum_i |A\H_i|/|A|
         =162/(D^2-epsilon^2)+1-(105/106)^2
         >16411/11236>5/4.                          (11)

The last strict gap in the limiting value is
16411/11236-5/4=1183/5618>0. Thus (11) persists as delta and c
tend to zero. At epsilon=1/100 the exact ratio is

    kappa=6146466463/4208252788,
    kappa-5/4=443075239/2104126394>0.

The verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_shifted_section_overlap_obstruction_defect_transport.py`
checks 57 exact rational identities and inequalities at that parameter,
including polygon convexity, all nine midpoint containments, equal cap
masses, moment cancellation, strict reflected-segment containment, and
the residual gap. The proofs above establish the whole parameter family
and do not rely on a numerical optimization.

The limitation is explicit: |K|>768 whereas |A|+|B|<5. The middle
fiber is heavy and its ordinary centroid already ensures OC. Nor has
global cap minimality across all continuous directions been proved.
This example therefore blocks only the suggested implication from
the listed local and fixed-normal geometric conditions to the overlap
budget; it is neither an OC counterexample nor a counterexample under
the additional no-heavy and genuine-global-criticality hypotheses.

## 7. Heaviness is forced already by the original endpoint pair

The previous example cannot be repaired merely by choosing a smaller
compatible middle fiber. The six vertices of A+B, in cyclic order, are

    (-9,-12),
    (8/5+epsilon,-7/5-epsilon),
    (8/5+epsilon,8/5-epsilon),
    (8/5-epsilon,8/5+epsilon),
    (-7/5-epsilon,8/5+epsilon),
    (-12,-9).

They are obtained by merging the cyclic edge directions of the two
triangles; equivalently they are six of the nine vertex sums and
their convex hull contains the remaining three. Shoelace expansion
gives

    |A+B|=681/10+(136/5)epsilon.

Therefore EVERY compatible middle fiber, before imposing any cap
condition, satisfies

    |K|-|A|-|B|
       >= |A+B|/4-a-9/2
        = 501/40-(72/5)epsilon >0.                 (12)

In mixed-area notation this is V(A,B)=159/5+3epsilon and the usual
planar identity |A+B|=a+b+2V(A,B). Formula (12) is proved here by
the displayed actual polygon and does not require that identity as
an unproved step. It identifies a concrete global geometric charge
that removes this local overlap obstruction under a no-heavy premise.
